analyst_observations: All 15 assertions pass for both skill versions — the assertions are non-discriminating at this level of granularity. Both versions correctly route to the right reference files and produce comprehensive answers.
Token usage is nearly identical (44374 vs 44399 mean) — the v0.3.0 SKILL.md is slightly shorter (210 vs 258 lines) but reference files are the same, so total context loaded is comparable.
Duration is comparable (97s vs 97s mean) with high variance driven by CI/CD eval (~130s both) which involves generating a complete bash script.

The key differences are QUALITATIVE, not quantitative: v0.3.0 produces more structured responses with better section headers, summary tables, and the Common Tasks examples in SKILL.md directly influence response patterns (particularly visible in CI/CD eval where the new skill's response closely mirrors the Common Tasks CI example).

The v0.2.0 decision tree (ASCII art) and v0.3.0 situation tables both successfully guide to the correct reference files — the routing mechanism change is a readability improvement, not a correctness one.
